skill.name: brand-guidelines
skill.description: Applies Anthropic-style brand colors, typography, and visual formatting guidance to documents, decks, and design artifacts.
skill.summary: Apply Anthropic-style colors, typography, and visual hierarchy to user-provided artifacts.
skill.author: 7Spade

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code around color values and a local RGBColor class reference. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or executable behavior was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - Dark: `#141413` - Primary text and dark backgrounds
- Light: `#faf9f5` - Light backgrounds and text on dark

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks delimit a hex color value in a Markdown list, not an executable shell or Ruby expression. The line provides design color guidance only.
The backticks delimit a hex color value for a light background, not command execution. No shell, Ruby, or user-controlled input is present.
The inline backticks wrap a gray color value used for brand styling. This is documentation text and does not invoke an interpreter.
The inline code marker is used to format a light gray color value in Markdown. There is no executable code path or command string.
The backticks wrap an orange accent color value. The surrounding text is a static brand color list, not shell execution guidance.
The backticks wrap a blue accent color value in documentation. No command, process launch, or interpreter syntax is present.
The backticks wrap a green accent color value in a Markdown list. This is a formatting false positive with no execution semantics.
Line 23 describes a mid gray brand color and secondary elements. It does not instruct the agent to inspect the system or gather host information.
The python-pptx RGBColor mention is implementation guidance for applying local color values. It contains no network scan, request, or discovery instruction.

content.value_statement: Brand styling can drift across documents, decks, and design artifacts. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code direct guidance for consistent visual formatting.
actual_capabilities: Lists primary and accent color values for Anthropic-style materials.
Defines heading and body font choices with fallback fonts.
Guides text styling by size, hierarchy, and background contrast.
Guides accent color use for non-text shapes.
Documents PowerPoint color application through python-pptx RGBColor.
limitations: Does not include scripts, templates, or image assets.
Requires the user or agent to apply guidance to a target artifact.
Best typography results require Poppins and Lora to be installed.
Does not verify current legal or trademark approval for brand use.

use_cases.title: Style a Presentation
use_cases.description: Apply consistent colors, fonts, and accent shapes to a slide deck before review.

use_cases.title: Prepare Design Handoff Notes
use_cases.description: Convert brand styling rules into clear instructions for visual designers or document editors.

use_cases.title: Review Document Consistency
use_cases.description: Check a report or proposal for font, color, and hierarchy changes that match the guide.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Basic Styling
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a direct style pass.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the brand guidelines to this slide deck. Use the listed colors, fonts, and accent rules. Keep all existing content.

prompt_templates.title: Review Brand Consistency
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review before sharing a document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this document for brand consistency. Identify text, color, and shape changes needed to match the Anthropic style guide.

prompt_templates.title: Create Formatting Instructions
prompt_templates.prompt: Create step-by-step formatting instructions for this artifact. Include heading, body text, background, and accent treatment recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Full Visual Refresh
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a structured redesign plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this multi-section asset and plan a full brand refresh. Prioritize readability, hierarchy, color balance, and consistent typography.

output_examples.input: A slide deck uses mixed fonts, bright accents, and inconsistent heading sizes.
output_examples.output: Headings use Poppins with clear hierarchy. Body text uses Lora. Accent shapes rotate through orange, blue, and green.

output_examples.input: A proposal needs a concise brand review before client delivery.
output_examples.output: The review flags off-brand colors, missing font fallbacks, weak contrast, and places where accent colors should be limited.

output_examples.input: A document editor needs handoff notes for a visual refresh.
output_examples.output: The notes explain font choices, color roles, background treatment, and shape styling in plain editing steps.

best_practices: Provide the target artifact and state the output format before requesting changes.
Install Poppins and Lora when exact typography matters.
Ask for a review pass after applying brand colors and font rules.
anti_patterns: Do not use the guide as legal approval for brand or trademark usage.
Do not apply accent colors to every element in a dense layout.
Do not expect the skill to generate source assets or install fonts.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps apply Anthropic-style colors, fonts, hierarchy, and accent rules to visual artifacts.

faq.question: Does it modify files by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance that Claude, Codex, or Claude Code can apply when working with user-provided files.

faq.question: Does it install fonts?
faq.answer: No. It recommends Poppins and Lora with fallback fonts, but it does not install software.

faq.question: Can it style PowerPoint decks?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide includes color guidance that can be applied with PowerPoint editing tools or python-pptx.

faq.question: Is it limited to presentations?
faq.answer: No. The guidance can support documents, reports, mockups, and other visual materials.

faq.question: Does it confirm official brand permission?
faq.answer: No. Users remain responsible for checking current brand, legal, and trademark requirements.
